children: Anthropic PBC (ANT) plans a Nasdaq IPO of 825 million shares at $70–$78, valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion. The book was over six times oversubscribed; trading is expected Nov. 19, pending approvals.
Anthropic PBC (ANT) faced investor questions during its IPO roadshow about sustaining its AI-model lead against Google and expanding Claude beyond coding, with some meetings offering limited answers.
Anthropic PBC (ANT) reportedly warned in a filing that escalating U.S.-China tensions and federal scrutiny of its exposure to Chinese state actors pose material risks to its business.
Several banks underwriting Anthropic PBC’s IPO reportedly may reject orders from mainland China and Hong Kong investors, citing U.S. defense-trade restrictions.
Anthropic (ANT) plans to enter new markets as its AI improves, CEO Dario Amodei said. He sees scientific research as a market larger than programming, a key revenue source today.
Anthropic PBC (ANT) faces a U.S. lawsuit from Global Printing, which alleges its AI model name “Mythos” infringes its trademark and seeks damages and a ban. Anthropic disputes the claims.
Eligible Interactive Brokers Ireland clients can apply for Anthropic PBC’s (ANT) IPO by Nov. 17 at 21:00 CET, with funds ready by the deadline. The offer spans nine European countries.
• Bill Ackman said he was impressed by Anthropic PBC (ANT) CEO Dario Amodei’s presentation at the company’s IPO roadshow event in New York.
